title: style: Lint documentation scss files
body: The linting task is currently only applied to the main code, not the documentation. This already created code regressions (https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/534), so we should enforce the same standard as in the main code.

comments.body:
I just spent 1 hour and it's really more complex than expected:
- because of Jekyll, the main S{A,C}SS files have a triple-dash `---` header -> breaks parsing
- I got plenty of errors because of some bugs of the `sass-lint` tool (undefined exceptions)

Not sure what to do in the short term.

Yes, me too. I spent some hours on it, I have a branch with part of the fix. I managed to fix the jekyll/front-matter issue and making all run, but now I have a huge list of linting errors in our doc scss files.

I'll push the branch shortly so you can have a look.
Pushed to #566. Linting of scss doc is enabled on this branch but fails loudly (176 errors detected)
OK, I would keep that out of 1.0 then; it looks like we're gonna spend days on it :)

Yep, I realized as well that this was going to take some time so I dumped it here as a WIP so you could see it.

We'll have to be extra careful in the CSS editing of the docs because we have no linting on it.
What I don't understand is that guard will scream if there is some error. no?
Apparently not. I managed to commit `sass` files in the past that could not compile correctly
It won't prevent you to commit, but the terminal will say that the the sass compile is broken.
Yep, and we would like Travis to catch that
Yes all checks on travis otherwise it's only working if the dev has ran the good commands (= we do not trust DEVS :D)
